questions.prompt: GPIS D-01: what is the remark for a total of 79?

wrong.0: 79 does not round up. Highest starts at exactly 80.
wrong.3: High Average is 60–64, two bands lower.

questions.prompt: GPIS D-01: which pair tests one boundary correctly?
questions.why: 64 and 65 sit on the two sides of one edge, the start of High.

wrong.1: These are the lower edges of two different bands; neither edge is tested from both sides.
wrong.2: Both are inside one band, High.

questions.why: NaN is a special number value: "not a number" is still of kind number.

wrong.0: There is no kind called NaN.

questions.why: `>=` turns the text into a number first; `===` needs the same kind, and text is not a number.

wrong.0: `===` never converts. Text and number are different kinds.
wrong.2: `>=` does convert the text "80" to the number 80.
wrong.3: JavaScript does not refuse; it converts silently. That is the trap.

questions.prompt: Find the mistake: `if (s >= 0) return "Lowest"; if (s >= 40) return "Lower"; …`
options: The first test is true for every score, so every remark is Lowest
questions.why: The checks start at the bottom. Start from the top band, so the first true check is the right band.

wrong.0: `==` would match only whole edge numbers, and most totals none at all.
wrong.1: An early return inside `if` is normal.
wrong.3: A total of 90 would be called Lowest.

questions.prompt: Why does GPIS never store the remark beside the score?
options: It can always be worked out from the score, and a stored copy can disagree with it
Because text cannot be stored in a database
questions.why: One source of truth: the score. A stored remark could stay wrong after a scale change.

wrong.1: A word per score is tiny. Space is not the reason.
wrong.2: Databases store text all the time.
wrong.3: The remark is printed on the report card for parents to read.

questions.prompt: A remark function receives 140. Which behaviour is safest for a report card?
options: Refuse it (throw), so the wrong mark is found
Return the remark for 100 and write a log line
questions.why: A refusal is noticed at once. Every other choice prints something that looks normal.

wrong.0: It hides a wrong mark behind the best result.
wrong.2: A blank means "not assessed" (D-10). It would look like a missing score.
wrong.3: Nobody reads the log, and the card still shows a remark for a mark that does not exist.
